newsitem.title: USA: U.S. futures exchanges to pursue common banking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. futures exchanges to pursue common banking.

text.p: U.S. futures exchanges will announce a common banking initiative later Thursday, futures exchange officials told Reuters.

"We are actually discussing and will probably announce an agreement with other exchanges to pursue common banking," Daniel Rappaport, chairman of New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), said late Wednesday during a futures industry conference here.

Officials from other exchanges said an announcement was due at 1400 EST/1900 GMT Thursday. They said the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), the Board of Trade Clearing Corp and NYMEX were among the exchanges involved.
"We have a common banking agreement with the CME that will be rolled out this year," Rappaport said.
Patrick Thompson, NYMEX president, said common banking would streamline the "pay-and-collect" process and filter down into a common settlement bank.
"We expect across the industry that we'll save a fair amount of money in operational costs," Thompson said.
He said common banking differed from common clearing because exchanges under common banking do not assume any risk from other exchanges.
